reading.body:
Kentucky's tracked data center capacity stands at 5 MW across five facilities, a figure that reflects an early-stage market rather than a major hub for AI compute infrastructure.

The five facilities are spread across four locations: Hopkins County, Ivel, Florence, and Louisville. Only one facility, CyrusOne Florence, carries a recorded capacity figure, and that single site accounts for all 5 MW in the dataset. The remaining four facilities have no MW figures attached, so the true aggregate capacity is unknown and almost certainly higher than what the data can confirm. Two of the five are operated by named colocation providers, CyrusOne and Flexential, while the others lack operator attribution.

For AI workloads, which are power-dense and require significant electrical capacity at a single site, 5 MW of confirmed capacity is a modest number. Large AI training clusters routinely require hundreds of megawatts, and even inference deployments at scale demand sustained power that this dataset does not show Kentucky supplying in quantity. The data covers only facilities in this specific inventory and says nothing about on-site power sources, grid interconnection agreements, or any planned expansions.
